record.context_brief: critical exponent elliptic equation in three dimensions
record.original_question: Let Omega be the unit ball in R^3, let lambda_1 = pi^2 be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of -Delta on Omega, and consider smooth functions u: Omega -> R satisfying -Delta u = u^5 + lambda u in Omega and u = 0 on the boundary. For parameters 0 < lambda <= lambda_1/4, does there exist a nonzero solution u? If such a solution exists in this interval, the source notes that it cannot be positive and radial; it would have to be non-radial and sign-changing.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1.1 (Implicit in [30]). Assume that 0 < lambda <= lambda_1/4. Does there exist a solution u not identically zero of (1.1)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the open unit ball, and let $\lambda_1 = \pi^2$ denote the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ on $\Omega$. For a real parameter $\lambda$ with $0 < \lambda \le \lambda_1/4$, consider the boundary value problem
$$-\Delta u = |u|^4 u + \lambda u \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial \Omega,$$
where solutions $u : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ are sought in the classical (smooth) sense. Note that the nonlinearity has the critical Sobolev exponent $5 = (n+2)/(n-2)$ for $n=3$, and it is known that for $\lambda$ in this range any nontrivial solution must be non-radial and sign-changing. Determine whether there exists a solution $u \not\equiv 0$ to this problem for every $\lambda \in (0, \lambda_1/4]$.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint ("On Brezis' first open problem: a complete solution", arXiv:2503.06904) claims a complete resolution of this problem, establishing the existence of infinitely many sign-changing, nonradial solutions for the full range of the parameter on the three-dimensional ball, including the previously open regime $0 < \lambda \le \lambda_1/4$. The result is recent and pending peer-review confirmation, but it is presented as a complete solution to this open problem.

status_evidence.title: On Brezis' First Open Problem: A Complete Solution
status_evidence.snippet: a complete resolution to the first one--Open Problem 1.1--in Brezis's favorite open problems list: the existence of solutions to the long-standing Brezis-Nirenberg problem on a three-dimensional ball... existence of infinitely many sign-changing, nonradial solutions for the full range of the parameter
status_evidence.claim: The paper claims a complete resolution of the open problem, constructing nontrivial (sign-changing, non-radial) solutions for the full parameter range including 0 < lambda <= lambda_1/4.
